title: SSE idempotent-replay-flags and graceful client degradation plan
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Summary:
Several customers reported blurred/duplicated partial transcripts and missing final tokens when their web clients experienced transient upstream disconnects. Investigation shows a class of incidents where the gateway ACKing semantics were ambiguous during network flaps, causing duplicate replays or silent drops depending on timing. This ticket implements a cross-layer approach: (1) introduce an idempotent-replay flag and opaque replay_id on SSE sessions, (2) gate accepting replayed frames at the consumer layer by matching replay_id+sequence-range, and (3) add a graceful client-degradation mode that surfaces a deterministic 'finality' marker earlier so clients can surface a best-effort UI while background repair runs.

Goals:
- Prevent duplicate visible tokens for customers who reconnect after short disconnects.
- Ensure deterministic single-writer semantics for finalization of a stream.
- Provide operators and support with a concise runbook to resolve high-severity customer incidents quickly.

Background:
We observed ~12 escalations in last 90 days tied to transient edge proxy restarts. Root cause pattern: edge retransmits in-flight frames when upstream ACK windows are reset, then host runtime replays cached KV segments. Without a cross-layer idempotency check, clients either show duplicate tokens or drop the tail when a later commit supersedes earlier fragments. Existing fixes (checkpoint snapshots, prefix-KV caching) reduced frequency but not these edge timing races.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce replay_id opaque token per SSE session visible in initial event metadata
Add server-side gating to ignore replayed frame sequences when replay_id does not match the active session or when sequence already finalized
Client-visible finality marker event (event_type: finality_sentinel) emitted deterministically when server believes no more tokens will be appended
Automated e2e test simulating edge disconnect + replay shows zero duplicate tokens in 1k-fuzz iterations
Operator runbook documented and validated during oncall rota (playbook exercises passed)
design_notes: High-level design: 1) Replay_id is generated by the runtime per client connection (UUID v4) and is short-lived. It is returned in initial SSE 'session' event and stored in the client SDK as session.replay_id. 2) Each emitted chunk includes sequence_start and sequence_end indices. Consumers must accept a chunk only if (a) session.replay_id matches current session OR (b) server explicitly marks chunk as 'idempotent-merge' — a rare mitigation mode for dedup-tolerant clients. 3) Finality sentinel is emitted when the runtime commits a final checkpoint for the request or when the model emits eos token. This gives clients an earlier signal to flush UI state even if later background repair writes are ongoing. Trade-offs: replay_id prevents many races but requires change in SDKs and gateway headers; we provide a compatibility fallback that accepts old clients but logs a warning. Scope note: Private/Dedicated deployments will use the same flags via the private control plane; on-prem upgrades required to pick runtime-1.21 for full behavior.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature-gate behind runtime flag 'sse_replay_id' (canary tenants)
Phase 1: Deploy to 5% of hosted tenants; enable operational telemetry and alerting (duplicate_token_rate)
Phase 2: Expand to 50% after 48h no regressions; start gated client SDK release (JS/Go) with compatibility checks
Phase 3: Full rollout and mark feature GA; push guidance to Dedicated/Private customers via release notes
monitoring: grafana/dashboard/streaming-duplication: spike in duplicate_token_rate > 0.01% triggers P1 alert
sentry/issue-tag: replay_id_mismatch_count to identify mismatched client versions
trace-sample: attach replay_id and sequence-range for 1% of streaming requests for 72h after rollout
comments: 2026-03-01 - Triage: Assigned to Diego. Initial customer reports from customer A and customer B show duplicated final tokens after 5-10s network blips. Repro on staging with proxy restart reproduced 3/5 times.

2026-03-03 - Investigation: Added extra debug to edge-proxy to log retransmit windows. Hypothesis: proxy retransmits chunks without preserving 'session' marker causing runtime to accept as new connection. Decided to add replay_id at handshake level.

2026-03-05 - Design review: Presented approach to infra and SDK leads. Concern raised about compatibility with older SDKs; agreed to implement conservative fallback that logs a compatibility metric and gates GA until clients updated.
2026-03-07 - Implementation: Runtime PR opened (runtime#9821). Core gating implemented. Added sequence-range checks and finality_sentinel emission. Unit tests added for accept/reject logic.

2026-03-09 - QA: Runbook created and exercised on staging. Found race where proxy reused connection-id across restarts — added proxy change to include per-connection nonce. Edge PR opened (edge-proxy#447).

2026-03-10 - Customer comms: Sent interim note to impacted customers describing mitigation and ETA for staged rollout. Recommended temporary client-side idempotency handling for customers who can patch quickly.

2026-03-12 - Next steps: Begin Phase 1 canary deployment. Oncall notified. Post-deploy plan: monitor duplicate_token_rate and trace-samples for 72h. Prepare rollback plan that disables 'sse_replay_id' flag if any regression > baseline.
